US forces disable ship ‘attempting to run’ Iran blockade in Gulf of Oman | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera Skip linksSkip to Content Live Sign up Navigation menuNews Show more news sectionsAfrica
US military jet strikes stern of commercial cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman ‘without harming the crew’, CENTCOM says.
United States forces have disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew “ignored repeated warnings and attempted to run the ongoing naval blockade against Iran”, according to Central Command (CENTCOM).
A US military fighter jet struck the stern of the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica, also known as the Arika Sun, with a precision munition on Saturday, “fully disabling the ship’s propulsion without harming the crew”, CENTCOM said in a statement. The vessel was attempting to transit regional waters after “having previously departed an Iranian port”.

list 3 of 3Trump ‘may’ join Saudi strikes on Houthis after Riyadh airport attack
CENTCOM said its forces resumed their blockade against all ships “entering or departing Iranian ports on July 14”, disabling four commercial vessels and turning around 135 ships during “three months of strict enforcement”.
US forces also destroyed 10 tankers linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) “multibillion-dollar shadow network” over the same period, CENTCOM said.
US Senator Chris Murphy questioned the military strike, writing on X: “What is this all for? Why are taxpayers paying billions to hit commercial ships?”
“Apparently the goal is to gain leverage in order to convince the Iranians to let us pay them billions to return everything to the way it all was before the war,” the Democratic politician added. “What a disaster.”
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency acknowledged the incident on Sunday, saying that it had received “a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman” and that authorities were investigating.
Meanwhile, the IRGC said it struck a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz for attempting to take an “illegal route”, as Tehran seeks to enforce its own blockade on the vital waterway.
In a statement carried by official Iranian media, the IRGC claimed Iranian forces “have taken control of the administration of the strait”.
“In carrying out this mission, a few hours ago, a giant LPG carrier named NV Sunshine, owned by NatWit, which was attempting to transit via the illegal route south of the Strait of Hormuz, was struck,” the statement said.
The UKMTO said on Sunday that an outbound tanker in the strait was struck on the port side by an unknown projectile, causing a fire on board. The UK agency said crew members were reported safe, while the damage and environmental impact remained unknown at the time of the report.
Tehran has attempted to enforce control over the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Israel war on Iran, insisting that ships obtain permission to cross via its preferred routes. However, vessels have increasingly risked taking an alternative route hugging the strait’s southern coast.
The UK maritime agency said on Thursday that a vessel sailing 94km (58 miles) north of Madinat ash Shamal, off the north coast of Qatar, was struck by multiple projectiles, resulting in several casualties.
The agency did not specify the origin of the ship or the number of people killed or injured, adding that authorities were investigating the incident amid a recent rise in attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.
Ships in the Gulf attempting to cross the strait, which is the sole maritime route in or out of the oil-rich region, have faced repeated attacks since the US and Israel began the war in late February.
The Strait of Hormuz remains vital to the global economy, with about a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas passing through the passage before the war began.
